apply.q: How do I apply for a travel document?
apply.a: Applications are submitted through the service that handles the document. Applying for a Document Signer certificate and requesting personalisation files is done in ePass42.

verify.q: How is an electronic travel document verified?
verify.a: Receiving authorities verify a document against the certificates and revocation information published in the Public Key Directory.

delivery.q: Can I have my document delivered?
delivery.a: Yes. Approved applicants can order personalisation and postal delivery through the ePass42 platform.

partners.title: Trusted partners
partners.description: Personalisation and delivery of approved documents is carried out by the trusted partner below.

strexp.name: Strategic Explorations (StrExp)
strexp.description: Professional card personalisation and postal delivery for applicants who prefer not to write the personalisation file to a card themselves.

help.title: Role-based help page added
help.summary: The portal now includes a help page with step-by-step guidance for applicants, reviewers and certificate administrators.

chinese.title: Interface available in Chinese
chinese.summary: The portal can now be used in Chinese, with browser-language detection and a locale switcher.

sltd.title: Revoked documents published as hashes
sltd.summary: The Public Key Directory publishes revoked travel documents as SHA-256 hashes, so a document can be checked without exposing personal data.

dscIssuance.title: Document Signer certificate issuance is live
dscIssuance.summary: Applicants can request a Document Signer certificate; approved certificates are issued automatically and listed in the PKD.

pkdInterfaces.title: Public Key Directory available over REST, LDIF and LDAP
pkdInterfaces.summary: The PKD is published over REST, as an LDIF dump, and through a read-only LDAP layer for existing directory clients.

about.intro: The National Immigration Agency (NIA) is responsible for the movement of people across the network, the issuance of travel documents and the operation of the public key infrastructure.
about.mission: Our mission is to facilitate legitimate travel and migration while protecting the integrity of our documents and the security of the network.
about.mandateItem1: Issue electronic travel documents and maintain the trust chain used to verify them.
about.mandateItem2: Operate the Country Signing Certification Authority and the Public Key Directory.
about.mandateItem3: Manage entry, residence and departure at the border.
about.mandateItem4: Advise the Government on immigration and document security policy.

accessibility.title: Accessibility
accessibility.description: The accessibility commitment and conformance of the NIA portal.
body: The National Immigration Agency is committed to making this portal usable by everyone, regardless of ability or the technology they use.
The portal is built on standard HTML semantics, supports keyboard navigation and responds to the operating system's reduced-motion and colour-scheme preferences.
If you encounter an accessibility barrier, please contact us by email so that we can help and improve the portal.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.description: How the NIA portal handles privacy and personal data.
body: This portal is a static website. It does not use tracking cookies and it does not send personal data to third parties.
The portal makes no requests to the public internet: fonts, icons and scripts are all served from the same origin.
Where a service asks you to sign in or submit personal data, that data is handled by the service itself (for example ePass42) under its own privacy notice.

terms.title: Terms of use
terms.description: The terms governing the use of the NIA portal.
body: This portal is an official information service of the National Immigration Agency.
The information published here is provided in good faith. Fees, processing times and service details may change, and the applicable service is always authoritative.
External services linked from this portal are operated independently and are governed by their own terms.
